chunks: Ali, from his father, from Yahya ibn Abi Imran, from Yunus, from al-Reza (peace be upon him):

key_terms.نَحْوَهُ: Similar to it — a technical hadith expression indicating the text of this narration is equivalent in meaning to the one preceding it

ai.seo_question: What does 'nahwahu' mean in hadith collections such as al-Kafi?
ai.summary: This is a short referential hadith in which Imam Ali al-Reza (AS) confirms that his teaching on military jihad when Islam is under threat is essentially the same as narrated by Imam al-Sadiq (AS) in the preceding hadith. The phrase 'similar to it' (نحوه) is a classical hadith convention indicating that a parallel chain leads to equivalent content. The transmission chain — running through Ali ibn Ibrahim, his father Ibrahim ibn Hashim, Yahya ibn Abi Imran, and Yunus ibn Abd al-Rahman — represents one of the well-known reliable chains in al-Kafi.

en.hubeali:
Ali, from his father, from Yahya Bin Abu Imran, form Yunus, 
(It has been narrated) from Al-Reza<sup>asws</sup>,
